chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Wahb ibn Wahb, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: “If a woman dies while there is in her womb a child that is moving, she is to be cut open and the child brought out.” And he said concerning a woman in whose womb the child dies, and there is fear for her, he said: “There is no harm in a man inserting his hand and cutting it up and removing it, if the women are not able to deal gently with it.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Imam 'Ali عليه السلام, cited here as the source of the ruling
key_terms.النِّسَاءُ: the women, meaning female attendants who would ordinarily handle such matters
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman, specifically in the context of pregnancy and medical danger
key_terms.فَيُقَطِّعَهُ: then cut it up, referring to dismembering the dead fetus for removal when necessary
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm, indicating legal permissibility
key_terms.وَلَدٌ يَتَحَرَّكُ: a child that is moving, indicating signs of life in the womb
key_terms.يُدْخِلَ الرَّجُلُ يَدَهُ: a man may insert his hand, referring to a necessary medical intervention
key_terms.يُشَقُّ: she is to be cut open, referring to surgical opening for extraction

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pregnant woman dies while her child is still alive, or if a dead fetus endangers the mother?
ai.summary: This hadith presents legal rulings concerning difficult childbirth and death-related cases involving a pregnant woman and her child. It addresses extracting a living child from a deceased mother and permitting necessary intervention when a dead fetus endangers the mother.
